draft.title: Simple quadratic equations
card: An equation such as \(x^{2} = 49\) asks: which numbers, when squared, give 49? Squaring means multiplying a number by itself.
Both \(7 \times 7 = 49\) and \((-7) \times (-7) = 49\), because a negative times a negative is positive. So there are two solutions.
Take the square root of the number and write both signs: \(x = \sqrt{49}\) or \(x = -\sqrt{49}\). This gives \(x = 7\) or \(x = -7\).
draft.remember: A squared letter equal to a positive number has a positive and a negative solution.

a.why: Both \(6^{2}\) and \((-6)^{2}\) equal 36, so there are two solutions. Giving only \(x = 6\) forgets that squaring a negative number also gives a positive.
a.clue: Which numbers multiplied by themselves give 36?

b.q: A square garden bed in Orange has an area of 81 square metres, written \(s^{2} = 81\). Its side length \(s\) is a length. Which statement is correct?
opts: Two solutions exist, but only \(s = 9\) can be a length
Only one solution exists, which is \(s = 9\)
Two solutions exist, and both can be lengths
b.why: The equation \(s^{2} = 81\) has two solutions, \(s = 9\) and \(s = -9\). A length cannot be negative, so only \(s = 9\) fits the garden. It is still wrong to say the equation has just one solution.
b.clue: Solve the equation first, then ask which answers a length can be.

b.best: Two solutions exist, but only \(s = 9\) can be a length

problems.detail: The options say 'solutions exist' without saying 'of the equation'. A student could defend 'Only one solution exists, which is s = 9' as true of the garden problem. Saying 'The equation has two solutions…' would remove the ambiguity.

proposal.title: Simple quadratic equations
card: An equation such as \(x^{2} = 49\) asks: which numbers, when squared, give 49? Squaring means multiplying a number by itself.
Both \(7 \times 7 = 49\) and \((-7) \times (-7) = 49\), because a negative times a negative is positive. So there are two solutions.
Take the square root of the number and write both signs: \(x = \sqrt{49}\) or \(x = -\sqrt{49}\). This gives \(x = 7\) or \(x = -7\).
For example, \(x^{2} = 25\) gives \(x = 5\) or \(x = -5\). If \(x\) stands for a length, only \(x = 5\) fits, since a length cannot be negative, but the equation still has two solutions.
proposal.remember: A squared letter equal to a positive number has a positive and a negative solution.

a.why: Both \(6^{2}\) and \((-6)^{2}\) equal 36, so there are two solutions. Giving only \(x = 6\) forgets that squaring a negative number also gives a positive.

opts: The equation has two solutions, but only \(s = 9\) is a length
The equation has only one solution, which is \(s = 9\)
The equation has two solutions, and both can be lengths
The equation has two solutions: \(s = 40.5\) and \(s = -40.5\)
b.why: The equation \(s^{2} = 81\) has two solutions, \(s = 9\) and \(s = -9\). A length cannot be negative, so only \(s = 9\) fits the garden. It is still wrong to say the equation has only one solution, because \((-9)^{2} = 81\) too.
